newsitem.title: USA: Prosecutors charge ex-Astra USA CEO cheated firm.
newsitem.headline: Prosecutors charge ex-Astra USA CEO cheated firm.

text.p: Federal prosecutors Thursday charged the former president and chief executive officer of Astra U.S.A. with swindling his company of more than $1 million and failing to report the money on his tax returns.
Lars Bildman, who was dismissed from his job last April, "used the company like a personal piggy bank," Deputy U.S. Attorney for Massachusetts Mark Pearlstein told reporters.
Astra U.S.A. is a unit of Swedish pharamceutical company Astra AB.

Bildman and Astra U.S.A.'s former chief executive officer, Stefan Solvell, conspired to defraud the company as Bildman ordered extensive landscaping and renovations to homes in Boston, the indictment alleged.
Bildman was scheduled for a court hearing later on Thursday in Burlington, Vt.

Pearlstein said Bildman billed his company for his dalliances and vacations, reporting them as business trips. He also failed to report any of the benefits on his federal and state income tax forms for 1993, 1994, 1995, according to the 35-count indictment.

If found guilty, he faces up to five years in prison and a $250,000 fine for each count of conspiracy, mail fraud, wire fraud and interstate travel for prostitution. He faces up to three years in prison and a $250,000 fine on each count of the tax charges.
Prosecutors said Astra U.S.A. cooperated fully with the investigation, which is still continuing.

They credited a story in Businessweek, the company's own internal investigation and a series of lawsuits brought by former employes, who charged Bildman with sexual harassment, as sparking the criminal investigation.
When Astra dismissed Bildman it estimated its losses at about $2 million. Asked about the difference in sums, Pearlstein replied: "I can't comment except to say the investigation is continuing."
